text:
Scott Mayfield has played every one of his 617 NHL games for the Islanders, and right now he's struggling to get into the lineup. Yahoo Sports reported that Ben Hutton has supplanted him, and he's dressed for only six games, the last on Nov. 5 at under 9 minutes.

The odd part is that the Islanders have been good with him out there. They've taken 58% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five during his shifts, eight points better than without him, and scored nearly three more goals than those chances predicted. That second number is the lucky part; the share is more encouraging, though six games is a thin sample.

His game was never about offense. Evolving-Hockey had his team creating less with him on the ice than nearly any other defenseman last season (bottom 8%), and he hasn't recorded a point yet. What he does well is defend his blue line: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him stopping 17% of the entries aimed at him, against 11% for a typical defenseman. At 34, that's the skill that will decide whether he works his way back in.
headline: Scott Mayfield, an Islander for life, fights for a spot
